custom_logic_notes: EA uses OnBookEvent (depth of market change) as trigger, not OnTick. Entry: when no position and within trading hours and volume/spread filters pass, if last trade price >= ask+interval then BUY_LIMIT at ask; if last trade price <= bid-interval then SELL_LIMIT at bid. Reversal: when in a position, if outside trading hours or price crosses threshold against position, places opposite limit order. Uses a busy-wait loop (while PositionsTotal unchanged) after placing order: if DOM price moves away from order price, deletes pending order and retries. MarketBook (order book/DOM) data is essential - no standard indicator replacement. Time filter has complex multi-session schedule: 10:00:10-13:54:30, 14:08:30-15:44:30, 16:05:30-18:39:30, 19:15:10-23:44:30. Weekend (Sat/Sun) blocked. Morning session 00:00-10:00 blocked. Volume filter: last trade volume must be between minVolume and maxVolume. Magic number: 68975. Orders are DAY orders (ORDER_TIME_DAY).
python_conversion_notes: Requires tick-level L2/DOM data which is generally unavailable in Python backtesting frameworks. The busy-wait order management loop (delete-replace pending order on DOM price shift) cannot be replicated in vectorized backtesting. The signal source is SYMBOL_LAST (last traded price) vs DOM best bid/ask spread + interval threshold. To approximate in Python, would need: (1) tick data with bid/ask/last/volume, (2) spread filter, (3) multi-session time filter, (4) limit order fill simulation. The order-delete-replace loop for DOM price drift is broker-runtime behavior with no backtest equivalent. Recommend tick-by-tick simulation only.
